summary: We are testing whether a branch-and-bound (BnB) maximum clique solver with degeneracy ordering, greedy coloring bounds, and bitset-accelerated candidate intersection can achieve near-perfect scores (≥95/100) on the Maximum Clique problem with N≤1000, and whether this significantly outperforms a greedy-only baseline. This is iteration 1, establishing the core algorithmic mechanism.
key_points: h-main arm: BnB with degeneracy ordering + greedy coloring upper bound + bitset intersection + 500 greedy restarts for initial lower bound. Prediction: score ≥ 95. This is the standard exact/near-exact approach for max clique at this scale (N≤1000, 2s time limit).

h-control-negative arm: Greedy-only with 500 random restarts and degree-based ordering, no BnB search. Prediction: score < 85. This isolates the contribution of exhaustive BnB search vs. simple heuristic restarts.

Confirmation: h-main scores ≥ 95 AND meaningfully outperforms h-control-negative (≥10 point gap). Refutation: if both score similarly (greedy is sufficient) or if h-main scores low (BnB hits time limit or has bugs). Key diagnostic: if h-main is slow, check whether coloring bound is too loose or bitset operations have overhead issues.

Design is well-scoped: N≤1000 means bitsets fit in ~16 64-bit words, making BnB with bitset intersection very fast. The 1850ms time cutoff leaves a 150ms safety buffer. The approach is the gold standard for exact max clique at this graph size.
